title: Group 3 UAS MAGTF Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
1.     MOS 7315, Group 3 UAS MAGTF Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. UAS Officers employ a network enabled and digitally
interoperable UAS, from a Ground Control Station, to provide reconnaissance,
surveillance, targeting and acquisition (RSTA), aviation fires, and electro-
magnetic support across the full spectrum of combat operations. UAS Officers
will advise supported commanders on matters pertaining to UAS integration;
and provide information of intelligence value not readily available from
normal sources. UAS Officers are the supported commander’s subject matter
expert on UAS tactics, techniques, and procedures.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Security requirement: eligibility for top secret clearance with
sensitive compartmented information (TS/SCI).

        (3) Must meet the physical requirements per reference (ai), Manual of
the Medical Department, section IV, article 15-100.

        (4) Must take the aviation standard test battery (ASTB) and score
a four or higher on the academic qualification rating (AQR) and a six or
higher on either the pilot flight aptitude rating (PFAR) or the flight
officer flight aptitude rating (FOFAR).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the requirements for Basic Unmanned Qualification IV
(BUQ-4) in accordance with CJCSI 3255.01 by any of the following methods:

                (a) Complete the USAF Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPA) Course:

                1. Pilot Flight Screening Course (C70RPB1), at USAF Air
Education and Training Command, Pueblo, CO.

                2. Remotely Piloted Aircraft Instrument Qualification (RIQ)
Course (F16RPA4) at USAF 558 FTS, Randolph AFB, TX.

                3. Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPA) Fundamentals Course (RFC)
(F16RPC4) at USAF 558 FTS, Randolph AFB, TX.

            (b) Complete Student Naval Aviator (SNA) Primary Flight Training
(CIN Q-2A-0416 or Q-2A-0417) through the instrument phase.

            (c) Complete Student Naval Flight Officer (SNFO) Primary I
Training Course (CIN Q-2D-0162).

        (2) Designated Naval Aviators and Naval Flight Officers have met the
BUQ-4 requirements.

        (3) A BUQ-4 individual will be awarded the MOS 7315 after the
completion of the following course: RQ-21A Course (M04TACD) at the RQ-21
FRD, MCAS Cherry Point, NC.




                                          1-270                      Enclosure (1)
 1142                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



       d.   Duties

        (1) Provides air support through UAS Level 4 (function and control of
unmanned aircraft and payload minus takeoff and landing) and/or UAS Level 5
(full function and control of unmanned aircraft and payload)
interoperability.

        (2) Perform electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO) against enemy
communications, RADAR, and cyber networks; plans and executes multi-sensor
imagery reconnaissance and surveillance over assigned areas; advises,
coordinates, and controls supporting arms on behalf of the supported
commander; and when directed, destroys targets through kinetic or non-kinetic
means.

        (3) Performs the duties as a member of the supported commander’s
Cyber Electronic Warfare Coordination Cell (CEWCC).

            (4) Executes offensive and defensive tactics.

            (5) Supervises analysis, synthesis, and dissemination of information.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders/Managers, All Other
55-1019.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
